claims.text: Pack-cementation aluminizing will enrich the surface of the HEA bond coat with aluminum.
Surface aluminum enrichment will promote in-situ formation of an Al2O3 layer during high-temperature exposure.
The aluminizing treatment will produce a dense and continuous alumina scale.
The resulting alumina scale will adhere well to the underlying HEA bond coat.
An adherent alumina scale will reduce oxide spallation.
Introduced aluminide species will react with oxygen to form alumina during high-temperature exposure.
The alumina scale formed by the treatment will be thermodynamically stable and slow-growing.
The alumina scale will act as a barrier to further oxidation.
The alumina scale will minimize defect formation and spallation at the TBC interface.
Aluminized HEA bond coats will have a higher cyclic-oxidation cycle life than untreated HEA bond coats.
Aluminized HEA bond coats will have a lower spallation rate than untreated HEA bond coats.
Untreated HEA bond coats experience oxidation-induced degradation and coating spallation during cyclic high-temperature exposure.
The durability improvement should remain effective in oxidizing cyclic-exposure environments up to approximately 1200°C.
The improvement is not expected to remain effective above the stated alumina-stability range or in a reductive environment.
Aluminizing treatments have a generally beneficial effect in alloy systems other than the proposed HEA bond coats.
The multicomponent nature of the HEA may affect alumina-scale thickness, adhesion, or growth kinetics.
